topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of cancer causation and sets out the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: endogenous mutations versus environmental influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises through an interplay of endogenous mutational processes, environmental exposures, and inherited predispositions as shown by epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Biological and chemical mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific biochemical and cellular mechanisms through which infectious agents, chemical mutagens, radiation, and tumor promoters drive malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine and validate whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Summary and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing key takeaways on environmental cancer risks and everyday decision-making.
